subject.title: bug(slack): slash commands (/compact /new /stop) are silently inert in Slack DMs — no recovery path for wedged sessions

question: For Slack DMs with `dmPolicy: open`, should text recovery commands be authorized for every admitted DM sender, only command-owner allowlisted senders, or visibly denied unless command-authorized?
rationale: The source shows admission and command authority are separate, and broadening recovery commands changes who can compact, reset, or stop sessions from Slack DMs.

options.title: Owner-only with visible denial
options.body: Keep recovery commands restricted to command-authorized senders and send a clear Slack reply when an admitted DM sender tries an unauthorized recovery command.

options.title: Admitted DM recovery commands
options.body: Allow admitted Slack DM senders to run a narrow set of session recovery commands while keeping broader owner-only commands restricted.

options.title: Redirect Slack text commands
options.body: Disable Slack DM text recovery command execution and reply with the supported native command or CLI recovery path.

recommendation.title: Owner-only with visible denial
recommendation.body: Keep recovery commands restricted to command-authorized senders and send a clear Slack reply when an admitted DM sender tries an unauthorized recovery command.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest current-source signal across the Slack preparation and generic channel command-context surfaces involved in the decision.
